rankingLogic: Weighted by site rank 5. (1) indexability contradiction on an indexed page: NONE found. (2) Phase-A/standard finding on a page Phase B says is striking-distance/low-CTR/top-clicks. (3) template finding affecting many pages on a trafficked site. (4) CWV over threshold on a ranked template: NONE (LCP 0.92s). (5) everything else; zero-impression pages and bulk notices demoted.
verdict: Clean technical + AEO foundation (0 crawl errors, LCP 0.92s, strong JSON-LD, llms.txt, robots/AI policy all pass); the entire opportunity is converting the /league-id cluster's thousands of position-8-to-10 impressions - currently ZERO Google clicks - into traffic, starting with the hub-vs-child ESPN cannibalization.

suggestions.title: Resolve /league-id hub vs /league-id/espn cannibalization on ESPN queries
suggestions.evidence: GSC cannibalization: 'how to find espn league id' - hub 178 impr @8.60 + /espn child 64 impr @8.69, 0 clicks (242 impr total, clickShareConflict 1); 'how to find league id on espn' - hub 54 impr @9.37 + /espn 129 impr @8.52, 0 clicks. Confirmed in source: the hub hero (page.tsx lines 62-73) itself answers the ESPN question ('On ESPN? Your league ID is the number after leagueId=...') and HUB_FAQS names ESPN, so Google ranks both URLs and splits the signal. Both indexed (inspection PASS).
suggestions.fix: Make /league-id/espn the single ESPN target. On the hub, demote the ESPN-specific answer in the hero to a generic one-liner that links to the child, and drop ESPN specifics from HUB_FAQS; keep the hub targeting the generic/multi-platform term ('fantasy league id finder') and funnelling down. Concentrating the signal lets one page climb instead of two stalling at pos 8-9.

suggestions.title: Answer-first + exact-phrase titles on the league-id child pages to lift the pos-5-to-10 zero-click cluster
suggestions.evidence: GSC low_ctr: 'how to find sleeper league id' /league-id/sleeper pos 5.29, 162 impr, 0 clicks (benchmark 4%); 'where to find sleeper league id' pos 4.99, 85 impr, 0 clicks. low_hanging_fruit estimates ~178 recoverable clicks across the ESPN+Sleeper set. These are genuine page-1 positions earning nothing, so the snippet is losing the click to a SERP feature or an official platform page. NOTE the SAME pages earn clicks on Bing at pos 3-5 (bing page_stats: /league-id/espn 3-13 clicks/wk), so the content is fine - this is Google SERP/snippet competition.
suggestions.fix: For the pos-5 Sleeper page, lead the first visible line with the literal answer and the ID shape ('Your Sleeper league ID is the 18-digit number after /leagues/ ...'), already in the description - mirror it as the opening sentence of the rendered intro so Google can lift it as a snippet. Keep titles leading with the exact query phrasing + year (Sleeper title already does). Realistic ceiling: backlinks are near zero (see rank 6), so expect snippet/CTR gains more than large rank jumps.

suggestions.title: Add an /about (maker + open-source) trust entity for E-E-A-T and AI citability
suggestions.evidence: standard H4: no /about, /methodology, /editorial-policy page; H3: no /authors page (the one Article carries author:true but there is no author entity page). Methodology itself is well covered by /why-fair, /how-it-works and /guides/is-your-draft-order-actually-random, so the real gap is a who-runs-this trust entity. For a 'the open source is the trust story' product, an author/maker page that states, answer-first, who maintains it and links the randomizer at its commit SHA is exactly what AI engines cite.
suggestions.fix: Add a short /about page: who maintains it, the open-source randomizer linked at the exact commit (src/lib/randomizer.ts + GITHUB_URL), and the trust claim stated first. Wire Organization/Person JSON-LD. Do NOT build the multi-engine AEO measurement loop (user-punted).

suggestions.title: Extend 7 short meta descriptions to the 150-160 band
suggestions.evidence: text-length.mjs (rendered): why-fair 130, mfl 142, how-it-works 144, league-id/fleaflicker 147, fantasy-football 148, guides/commissioner-guide 123. All title lengths are fine (<=60). The /p/* dynamic wheel descriptions are short too but are by-design user content, not static pages - skip those.
suggestions.fix: Lengthen each to 150-160 rendered chars with a concrete second clause (platform, what the ID looks like, or the trust claim). clampMeta already guards the upper bound.

suggestions.title: Per-route OG images for the marketing pages (share/social CTR)
suggestions.evidence: standard D1 (partial): og:image on 12/12 but only 2 distinct images across 6 families - every marketing page shares the global /opengraph-image. The draw and wheel pages (/d, /p) already render per-route podium/result cards; the marketing cluster does not. Sharing is this product's whole distribution model, so a generic card is a missed loop.
suggestions.fix: Add a dynamic opengraph-image.tsx at the league-id and guides family roots (reuse the home card template, swap title/subtitle per route). Satori gotcha: explicit display on any element with >1 child (see CLAUDE.md).

suggestions.title: Thin backlink profile is the ceiling on the league-id cluster (off-repo, context)
suggestions.evidence: Bing get_link_counts TotalPages 0, Links []; GSC referringUrls are all internal (homepage/guide->page), InLinks 3. With essentially no external links, the league-id pages are capped around pos 8-9 regardless of on-page work. standard M1/M2 also fail: no docs/seo/growth-plan.md and 0 page-plans - the place to record a link/outreach plan.
suggestions.fix: This is not a code fix. Record a link-earning plan (Reddit r/fantasyfootball answers that cite the league-id pages, platform-help roundups) in docs/seo/growth-plan.md and per-page intent in docs/seo/page-plans/. Treat ranks 1-2 as the on-page prerequisite that makes any earned link pay off.

suggestions.title: Immutable cache-control on hashed _next/static assets
suggestions.evidence: standard I2 (partial): /_next/static/chunks/0-ignp5_6-le6.css served 'public, max-age=0, must-revalidate' - a content-hashed asset should be 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'. Security headers present (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options). Low impact because performance is already 100 and LCP 0.92s, but it is free repeat-visit bandwidth.
suggestions.fix: Set immutable long-max-age caching on /_next/static/* in the OpenNext/worker asset headers. Verify with wrangler dev (not preview), per CLAUDE.md.

card routes are share-image (PNG) endpoints, correctly excluded from the sitemap.
